transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alex Ramos (CSM) -- Carlos Rivera (Acme Head of ML), Leah Bennett (Platform Eng), Tom Wu (Security)

Summary (auto): quick onboarding status; access blockers (IAM/KMS/VPC); review initial perf samples; plan benchmark window and next steps.

Topics: onboarding checklist, access & roles, KMS, perf results, next steps

00:00 Jordan: okay team thanks for joining, we're at the usual weekly POC sync for Acme, I think everyone can hear me?
00:05 Carlos: yep, loud and clear, thanks Jordan.
00:18 Priya: hi all, Priya here, I'll run through environment readiness and the perf notes we collected from the test runs last week.
00:30 Jordan: quick agenda — 1) blocked items for onboarding, 2) share the perf summary 3) plan benchmark window and tasks. Anything to add?
00:38 Leah: just the VPC peering status, otherwise that's fine.
00:42 Alex: and I'll capture next steps / owners.

01:05 Priya: okay first, access: we still need the cross-account IAM role from Acme to attach the Redwood Private agent into your VPC. Leah, you had said you were provisioning that?
01:18 Leah: yes we started it yesterday, but Tom found a KMS policy question so we paused before sharing the ARN. The role is otherwise ready but we need to finalize the trust policy.
01:30 Tom: correct, security wants to limit STS assume-role to specific subnets and enforce CMK usage for logs. I sent an email but I can share the exact policy snippet now.
01:44 Priya: perfect — for the POC we only need assume-role permission and the ability to attach the ENI; we can do the CMK lock later but we do need a test key so Redwood can encrypt cache snapshots.
01:55 Jordan: to reiterate, we don't need production-level restrictions for the perf window; a temporary test key is fine as long as Tom approves.

03:10 Carlos: on the perf samples — last week we ran ~100k tokens across mixed short and long prompts, average p95 latency was ~420ms on the hosted variant and ~260ms on the dedicated-ish config you suggested. Note some tokens spiked when context size hit 8k.
03:30 Priya: yeah, those spikes look like KV cache misses and the attention kernel falling back to a slower path. We saw similar in our lab runs when sequence length distribution shifted.
03:44 Leah: can you remind me — is that the Redwood Dedicated or the Hosted API you used for that run? The sheet mixed labels a bit so it's hard to tell.
03:54 Priya: sorry that's my fault — the sheet labeled them 'Redwood Hosted' and 'Dedicated (small pool)'. The faster numbers are from the Dedicated pool (2x A100s), hosted was our multi-tenant routing.
04:12 Jordan: note there's a small typo in the sheet — "Redwood Delicated" — which confused us earlier.

05:05 Carlos: thanks, that clears it up. On costs, the estimated per-1k-token unit for dedicated is lower but there's the reserved commit math, which we need to finalize for a pilot.
05:20 Jordan: yep tradeoff is predictability and cost per token vs upfront commit. We'll put together a model for the pilot tier that matches your traffic shape.

06:00 Priya: about environment readiness checklist — items still open: 1) cross-account IAM role, 2) test KMS key, 3) Security review signoff for egress rules, 4) sample dataset and traffic profile for perf window.
06:20 Leah: dataset is ready; I'll upload S3 pointer to the shared slate. The traffic profile is the 70/30 short/long mix we discussed.
06:32 Tom: egress rules — we want to ensure the agent can only reach Redwood endpoints via the approved NAT path, and we need logging to our SIEM. Can Redwood provide the IP ranges or do you prefer FQDN allowlists?
06:46 Jordan: we can support both; for the POC IP ranges are easier but they'll change, so FQDN with TLS is acceptable for Acme if you prefer. We'll also ship a small logging sidecar that pushes to your SIEM endpoint.

08:10 Carlos: a few places where the transcript had mislabels earlier — in the perf sheet "K V cash" was listed, that's KV cache; just confirming that's what you mean.
08:22 Priya: yes KV cache, apologies for the stutter in the doc. We noticed the cache hit rate dropped when the prompt prefix changed frequently. That suggests we should instrument prefix bucketing in the next run.

09:01 Leah: what do you need from us to enable the prefix/caching improvements?
09:08 Priya: mostly pattern labels in the sample set and sticky session keying, which requires us to set a header in the request. We can provide the SDK snippet and a simple test harness.
09:20 Jordan: Priya will send that snippet after the call.

10:30 Carlos: on security/compliance — we reviewed the SOC2 summary last month but we do need the architecture diagram showing where logs and keys live. That doc will be important for our audit.
10:42 Jordan: understood, I'll share an updated infra diagram and SOC2 attestation PDF.

12:15 Tom: quick question about model variants and graceful fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity is transiently saturated, can requests fall back to hosted with a slight latency increase? We need that for availability SLOs.
12:30 Priya: yes, our smart routing can fallback to a compatible hosted model or a lower-cost quantized variant. We'll show a routing policy example — there are latency and cost tradeoffs we can tune.
12:46 Carlos: is there any data plane difference we should be aware of? For example, request headers or serialization changes?
12:54 Priya: surface is the same REST/SDK; the only difference is model name and the cache behavior. If you pin model versions we keep that consistent across variants.

15:05 Alex: capturing action item — Priya to run perf window; Jordan to send docs; Leah/Tom to share IAM/KMS.

16:00 Priya: about the perf window — we propose a 2-hour run next Tuesday where Redwood will run 200k tokens with the traffic mix; we can collect p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates. Does that work?
16:15 Leah: next Tuesday fine for me but I need to sync with platform team — can we set a tentative slot and confirm by Friday?
16:25 Jordan: will do, scheduling tentative 2025-12-16 16:00 UTC. Priya will confirm once we have the role and KMS.

18:00 Carlos: one blocker — our compliance team insists on per-token logging redaction before logs leave our VPC, can Redwood support partial redaction?
18:12 Priya: yes we support configurable redaction hooks and can run the sidecar inside your VPC before logs are forwarded. We'll document required fields and sample config.

20:30 Tom: also can we get a short runbook for incident response during the perf window? If something goes sideways we need to be able to rollback and revoke roles quickly.
20:44 Jordan: absolutely — we'll include a runbook and a short playbook for role revocation / throttling.

22:10 Carlos: curious on the quantization note — you mentioned a smaller quantized variant, any quality regressions we should expect on long-context summarization?
22:28 Priya: quantized variants can slightly degrade some tasks, long-context summarization sometimes shows minor hallucination shifts. We'll include a set of eval prompts and metrics so you can decide. If it's critical, we recommend running quality evals pre/post.

25:00 Leah: what's the expected time to onboard the Redwood Private agent once we give the role and KMS access?
25:12 Priya: typically 24-48 hours for initial attach and smoke tests, maybe a day longer if network approvals take time.
25:24 Jordan: so realistically POC perf run could happen 48-72 hours after we have role + key.

27:00 Carlos: great. On pricing — can you send a pilot pricing sheet that shows both hosted and a 3-month dedicated commit example? We want to model total cost of ownership.
27:15 Jordan: yes I'll include a cost model template in the follow-up email.

30:00 Priya: quick note on metrics we'll deliver after the run: raw logs, aggregated latency buckets (p50/p95/p99), token counts, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rates, and a short quality summary vs baseline.
30:18 Leah: that's perfect.

33:00 Alex: any other blockers?
33:06 Tom: one more small thing — SSO/SAML integration for the console. We need to test RBAC mappings as part of the pilot.
33:16 Jordan: we can provision a demo SAML config; Priya will send steps and a sample metadata XML.

35:00 Carlos: okay recap — Jordan send SOC2 + arch diagram + pricing; Priya send SDK snippet, runbook, perf schedule; Leah/Tom share role/CMK and confirm egress rules; schedule perf window tentatively 2025-12-16 16:00 UTC.
35:30 Leah: I'll aim to share the STS role ARN by Friday.
35:40 Tom: I'll confirm KMS access by Saturday.

36:00 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the items and share the calendar invite.
36:05 Carlos: thanks all.
36:10 Priya: thanks, bye.
